acceptance_criteria: AC-1 Backup, inventory and configuration collection each refuse a management_server device with the same code.
AC-2 The reason names the missing gate, not merely the role, so an operator reading it knows why nothing was issued and what would have to exist first.
AC-3 The refusal precedes every vendor, allowlist, credential and admission check; a test proves a management server is refused even when it would also have failed one of those.
AC-4 A gateway device is unaffected: its existing refusals fire in their existing order with their existing codes.
AC-5 No job is admitted, and no command is issued, for a refused device.
AC-6 The ui2 service tests pass with the new tests, and the repository privacy gate passes.

baseline.authority: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_14I_ARTEFACT_LOCATION_OPERATOR_RETRIEVAL_DEVIATION_AND_MANAGEMENT_SERVERS.md -- FROZEN, Product Owner directives 2026-09-14. MS-2: inventory, configuration and backup are collected from management servers with their own per-vendor read sets, measured and gated exactly as the gateway ones were, and nothing is issued against one until its own gate entries exist. MS-4: those read sets carry known constraints -- a Check Point management export is a long, heavy class-1 operation an open management client can block, and a Panorama configuration is large and must be streamed -- so a management-server capability is a separate movement with its own pilot device. MS-5: until MS-2's gates exist, a management server is a device that can be discovered from and confirmed, and whose collection actions are refused with a reason naming the missing gate.
baseline.engineering_baseline: The three collect services share one refusal shape and each already refuses an unsupported vendor before doing anything else.
baseline.product_baseline: Devices are added, enrolled and confirmed. Inventory, configuration and backup collection are admitted per device through three services that already refuse for other reasons. A device now carries a role, gateway or management_server, and every existing row is a gateway.
baseline.test_baseline: The ui2 service test suite passes on origin/main today.

invariants: Nothing is issued against a management server. A refusal is the whole behaviour.
Fail-closed: an unrecognised role is not treated as a gateway.
The refusal names the gate, never a raw address, hostname or credential.
A gateway device's admission path is byte-for-byte what it is today.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not open a pull request and does not merge.
report.objective: Refuse collection against a management server, naming the gate that is missing. Record 14I MS-2 forbids issuing anything against a management server until its own command gate entries exist, and none do. MS-5 says such a device may still be added, discovered from and confirmed, but its collection actions are refused with a reason naming the missing gate. NXS-LOCAL-0187 gave the device model the role this needs; nothing yet reads it.
output_contract: A management server can be added and confirmed, and the product refuses to collect from it in words that say what is missing.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One check in three services that already share a refusal shape; the model field exists and the clause states the behaviour exactly.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
The gradle command runs from ui2; the privacy gate runs from the repository root.
Every changed file names the clause it implements (14I MS-n).
Run only the commands named above.
Run `git diff --check origin/main` before every commit and fix what it names.
Leave the worktree clean: write reports outside the repository or remove them before closing.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is only for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the pull request or code comments.
Commit early and often on your lane.
The SESSION_CLOSE quotes the refusal reason you wrote and says where in each service the check sits.
risks: Placing the check after the vendor or allowlist test, which would let a management server of a supported vendor reach a capability lookup before being refused.
Writing a reason that names the device rather than the gate, which tells the operator what they can see already and not what is missing.
Treating an unexpected role value as a gateway, which fails open on exactly the axis this movement exists to close.

in: All three collect services refuse a device whose role is management_server, with one shared refusal code and a reason that names the missing gate in words an operator can act on: that the device is a management server, that its per-vendor read set has not been measured or gated yet, and that this is why nothing was issued. Follow the wording style of the refusals already there -- they cite their clause and say plainly what was refused and why.

The refusal is positioned so it cannot be reached around: after the device is found, and before any vendor, allowlist, credential or admission check, because none of those questions apply to a device the product may not touch at all.
Tests for each of the three services: a management_server device is refused with that code; a gateway device is unaffected and still reaches its existing checks in their existing order.
out: Any read set, command, route or capability for a management server. MS-2 forbids issuing anything until its own gate entries exist, and this movement creates none.
Any change to discovery or to the enrollment and confirm paths. MS-5 keeps a management server discoverable and confirmable; only collection is refused.
Any change to the existing refusal codes, their order relative to each other, or their wording.
Any change to the device model, to migration V21, or to the role vocabulary.
Any UI change. Showing the refusal is a separate movement.
